title: Rapid and quantitative detection of the inflammatory marker neopterin based on a visible luminescent Zn(II)–Eu(III) nanocluster

synthesis.procedure: Eu(OAc)3·6H2O, Zn(CF3SO3)2·4H2O and H2L were dissolved in EtOH, MeOH and DMF. Triethylamine in MeOH was added. The mixture was stirred under reflux in air for 30 min, cooled to room temperature, and subjected to slow vapor diffusion of diethyl ether. Yellow crystals formed after one month.

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.amount: 1 mL of a 1.0 mol/L solution in MeOH

solvents: MeOH (4 mL, plus 1 mL for triethylamine)
synthesis.time: 30 min reflux; crystals after one month
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Stirred reflux in air followed by slow vapor diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Cooled to room temperature; yellow crystals formed by diethyl ether vapor diffusion.

properties.summary: Compound 1 shows ligand-centered and Eu(III) emission. Neopterin enhances its 616 nm emission by more than tenfold and changes the observed emission from cyan to orange. Luminescence-based neopterin detection was demonstrated in acetonitrile, fetal calf serum and simulated urine.

measurements.name: 616 nm emission enhancement
measurements.conditions: Addition of 20 µM neopterin in CH3CN; excitation at 395 nm

measurements.name: Eu(III) emission intensity ratio I(5D0→7F2)/I(5D0→7F1)
measurements.conditions: With added neopterin at the reported 20 µM concentration

source_locations.location: X-Ray Crystallography section and Table S1

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The approximately 1.3 × 2.8 × 3.1 nm rectangular cluster comprises two equivalent Zn11Eu13 moieties linked by two Schiff-base ligands. Within each moiety, a carbonate anion bridges five Eu(III) and two Zn(II) ions.

material_class.structural_family: Gd(III) analogue of the Schiff-base-supported Zn(II)–Eu(III) nanocluster; no separate crystal structure reported

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the procedure reported for 1, substituting Gd(OAc)3·6H2O for the Eu reagent. The specified Gd, Zn and H2L reagents were combined using the same mixed-solvent, triethylamine-addition, reflux and cooling procedure. Yellow crystals were obtained after one month by slow vapor diffusion of diethyl ether.

properties.summary: The Gd(III) analogue was used for low-temperature emission measurements to estimate the Schiff-base ligand triplet excited-state energy; no separate sensing performance is reported for it.

measurements.conditions: Estimated from emission spectra of the Gd(III) analogue in CH3CN at 77 K; excitation at 395 nm
